about.title: Willows Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Willows is a small community, and many residents rely on the same handful of clinics and Glenn County providers for care. When something goes wrong during treatment, it can be hard to know whether it was an unavoidable complication or a preventable error. California law recognizes that not every bad outcome is malpractice — a claim generally requires showing a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that failure caused harm. Because these cases hinge on medical records and expert review rather than crash reports, timing matters: California's MICRA framework sets strict notice and filing deadlines. We review your medical records and can explain your options. If we take your case, we handle it on contingency — you pay no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Deadlines Are Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally gives one year from discovery of the injury, capped at three years from the date it occurred, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. Missing these steps can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm the standard of care was breached, arranging that review early is important to your case.

items.title: Damage Caps Change Over Time
items.desc: California's cap on non-economic damages rises annually under MICRA, so understanding current limits matters for your case.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Willows?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. A 90-day notice to the provider is also required before filing suit. We can confirm how these deadlines apply to your specific situation.

items.question: Is a poor medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a bad result alone doesn't prove negligence. A claim typically requires showing the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care and that deviation caused harm, which is why expert medical review is usually necessary.

items.question: Are there local hospitals or clinics in Glenn County connected to these claims?
items.answer: Willows residents often receive care through local clinics or nearby Glenn County facilities, and claims can involve any licensed provider, hospital, or specialist involved in your treatment. We can review where your care took place and who was involved.
